To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in the molecular gels the RMTD is the dominant mechanism of the NMR relaxation in a low-frequency region and it can be used to characterize the dynamics at the pore surfaces in molecular materials.

the molecular dynamics of the solvents confined in low molecular mass molecular gels are characterized by the reorientation of the solvent molecules in the vicinity of the gel surfaces and that this process is mediated by translational diffusion.
in the 1:1 gels the solvent dynamics is characterized by the RMTD mechanism and that the relaxation data for the confined solvent are well described by the two-phase fast exchange model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular dynamics at the liquid-solid interface in molecular gels.
the dynamics of confined solvents and it is shown that NMR relaxation dispersion data provide a unique insight into the dynamics of the solvent confined in molecular gels and in the bulk solvents.
the molecular dynamics of the solvents in the molecular gels formed with the aid of low molecular mass gelators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NMR relaxation of solvents in the molecular gels can be described by the two-phase fast exchange model.
the NMR relaxation of confined solvents in molecular gels is dominated by RMTD.

the RMTD is a dominating mechanism of the NMR relaxation of the solvent molecules in low-molecular mass gels and that this relaxation is sensitive to the relative dimensions of the gel pores and the surface layer of ordered gelator molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the molecular dynamics of the solvents in molecular gels is determined by the solvent-surface interaction and the solvent-gel interaction.
the solvent molecules are strongly bound to the surface of the gel pores, and the dynamics is governed by a reorientation process of the molecules in the surface layers.
the RMTD mechanism of the solvent dynamics at the pore surface is a general phenomenon for low molecular mass gelled solvents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RMTD relaxation mechanism of the confined solvents can be successfully applied to study the molecular dynamics of the solvents at the liquid-solid interfaces.
field-cycling NRM relaxometry can be used as a powerful tool in studies of dynamics of the confined solvents.
the field-cycling NRM relaxometry is an efficient method to identify the dynamic processes of the solute-solvent interactions at the solid-liquid interfaces.
